verdicts.title: activation_offloading copies model weights, not only activations, on every microbatch
verdicts.reasoning: Code chain verified line by line in the current tree. packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/torch/checkpoint/save_on_cpu.py:29-35 packs every saved tensor with `tensor.cpu()` and no size/role/alias test; the patch is live on the pinned torch (2.14.0+cu130) because native_support.saved_tensor_hooks_guard_scoped() returns False, so packages/.../checkpoint/__init__.py:52 calls save_on_cpu.apply(). _dp_trainer.py:1423-1430 builds `save_on_cpu(pin_memory=False)` when args.activation_offloading, and _dp_trainer.py:2204 wraps the whole `ctx.grad_fn(...)` (vmap(grad)+clip) in it. Reproduced the packing behavior on CPU with a saved_tensors_hooks probe: for nn.Sequential(Linear(64,256), ReLU, Linear(256,32)) under vmap(grad(functional_call)), 8 tensors are packed and the (256,32) second-layer weight (32768 B) is among them, packed unbatched -> once per grad_fn call regardless of microbatch size. Also reproduced the LoRA-shaped case: with only tiny adapters differentiated, every FROZEN base weight is still packed (needed for grad-wrt-input), ~1.5x the base parameter bytes per microbatch. So the mechanism the finding describes is real: enabling activation_offloading moves on the order of the (non-first-layer) parameter set device->host->device per microbatch, pageable, in addition to activations. TWO CORRECTIONS to the finding. (1) The first layer's weight is NOT saved (its input gradient is not needed), so the traffic is the parameter set minus the first layer, not literally every F.linear weight. (2) The 'dominant term' quantification is NOT established and its measurement is methodologically wrong: the cited 69,632 B / 94% figure counts tensor.numel()*element_size() as seen inside the functorch levels, i.e. per-example LOGICAL shapes. Unwrapping to the physical tensors (torch._C._functorch.get_unwrapped) shows activation tensors carry the microbatch dimension while the weight does not, so the weight share falls with microbatch size: on that same model I measured 36360 B total / 90% weight at B=1, 47136 B / 70% at B=4, 90240 B / 36% at B=16; in the LoRA probe 60% at B=1 vs 19% at B=8. Analytically the activation/weight ratio scales like microbatch*seq_len/hidden, so at realistic sequence lengths the parameter term is a meaningful but usually not dominant fraction. Severity lowered to low: performance only (affects_epsilon false, gradients verified identical with and without the hooks), reachable only via activation_offloading=True which defaults to False (_training_arguments.py:545), and already covered by an open tracked issue. DUPLICATE: issue #969 ('Make activation offload selective and overlap transfers', open, milestone Bazalt) cites the same two code sites, states the hook 'copies every saved tensor to CPU ... including small values, cheap-to-recompute tensors, parameter aliases', proposes exactly the fix sketched here ('selection policy based on tensor size, role/storage alias ... Keep parameter storage and tiny/cheap tensors on device'), and already records the same failure mode ('Offloading everything ... can be slower than reducing microbatch size'). PR #994 'perf(functional): make activation offload selective' is closed unmerged and the tree still has no policy. Not verified: any GPU wall-clock or PCIe measurement, and the host-RSS growth claim - no CUDA device is available in this environment.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: With activation_offloading=True (non-default), DPTrainer wraps the whole vmap(grad)+clip call in save_on_cpu(pin_memory=False). Because F.linear saves its weight whenever the gradient with respect to its input is needed, every parameter except the first layer's - including frozen base weights in a LoRA run - is copied device->host->device once per microbatch through pageable host memory, on top of the activations. Reproduced on CPU with a saved_tensors_hooks probe: unbatched weight tensors appear in the packed set and their byte volume is independent of microbatch size, whereas activation bytes scale with it (weight share of packed physical bytes: 90% at microbatch 1, 36% at microbatch 16 on a 2-layer MLP; 60% vs 19% in a LoRA-shaped probe). The consequence is wasted PCIe traffic on the order of the parameter set per microbatch that offloading was never meant to pay - a throughput regression, not a correctness or privacy defect - and it is a meaningful but generally not dominant fraction of total transfer at realistic sequence lengths. No GPU timing was measured.
